comments.body:
Two more of the same shape, found while reviewing #1167 by executing `setup()`, not fixed here:

- **`task: distill` with `modality: vision` or `audio`** trains text-only: the distill path never reads `modality`.
- **`task: sft` with `backend: unsloth` and `modality: vision` / `audio`** runs the transformers setup: the unsloth request is dropped for those modalities.

Both load without a word. Whoever takes this should decide per combination between a load-time refusal and real wiring, as above.

Part of this issue landed in #1193 (merged as `210298c8`), by @chiliec. Thank you: `task: distill` with `backend: unsloth` is now refused at config load with a message that names the reason and the supported backend, instead of being accepted and trained on transformers. The two remaining combinations (distill with `modality: vision`/`audio`, and sft on unsloth with vision/audio) stay open here and are @chiliec's, as follow-up PRs.

Hi @chiliec, thank you for #1193: you checked that no shipped config pairs distill with unsloth before refusing it, and you ran the review's mutation yourself before saying the test was fixed. #1202 and #1308 since then have been just as careful.

We are checking in on the follow-ups from #1186 that were handed to you on 2026-09-24 (no comment or branch for them yet). Nothing is owed and no explanation is needed. What is still open here:

1. `task: distill` with `modality: vision` or `audio` trains text-only, because the distill trainer never reads `modality`. Refuse it at config load, or wire it.
2. `task: sft` with `backend: unsloth` and `modality: vision` or `audio` runs the transformers setup: the vision and audio branches in `SFTTrainerWrapper.setup()` come before the unsloth one. Refuse it at config load, or wire it. Items 1 and 2 are separate PRs, as agreed on #1193.
3. The "Tip: unsloth is installed. Add backend: unsloth" line printed by `soup train` (`src/soup_cli/commands/train.py`, near line 1515) still shows for every task on the transformers backend. It should be gated on `UNSLOTH_SETUP_TASKS`; @Srinivasan8888's #1372 left it alone on purpose, for you.

A one-line answer is plenty: "still on it", "need a week or two", "taking only item N", or "releasing it" are all fine.

If we have not heard by 2026-10-09, we will release the open items in this thread. Nobody is blamed, and everything you have already written stays credited if someone else continues.

Hi @chiliec, following the check-in of 2026-10-02 (no comment or branch since), the follow-up items handed over on 2026-09-24 are released, as described in CONTRIBUTING, so that someone else can pick them up. #1193 stays yours, and nothing is lost: if you want any of the items back, say so in a comment.

For anyone else: the items listed in the 2026-10-02 comment above are open; items 1 and 2 are separate PRs. Comment here with a short plan before starting.
Hi, sorry for the silence. I'd like to take item 3 back, PR today. Items 1 and 2 are free for others.
Thanks, @chiliec: item 3 is yours again and the `claimed` label is restored; #1782 is in review. Items 1 and 2 stay open for anyone, as you say.

#1782 (merged as `34a7b38e`), by @chiliec, closes out item 3 of this issue together with #1746 (feec5c6d). Thank you.
`soup train` prints the "unsloth is installed" tip only when the config would still load with `backend: unsloth`, which covers every task outside `UNSLOTH_SETUP_TASKS` and also `freeze_layers`, `rope_scaling_type` and `moe_lora` (#1746). #1782 pins it with three `soup train --dry-run` tests: the tip is printed for `sft` and not for `distill` or `classifier`. unsloth was not really installed in these tests; the check is stubbed.
This issue stays open. Where the items stand:

| Item | State |
|---|---|
| 1. `task: distill` with `modality: vision` or `audio` trains text-only | open |
| 2. `task: sft` with `backend: unsloth` and `modality: vision` or `audio` runs the transformers setup | open |
| 3. the "unsloth is installed" tip is printed for tasks with no unsloth setup | fixed by #1746, tests in #1782 |

Claim metadata update: item 3 is completed by #1746 and #1782, as recorded above, so the completed slice no longer reserves this aggregate issue. The stale `claimed` label is removed. Items 1 and 2 remain open and unclaimed; this is not a closure of those modality defects. The merged contribution stays credited to @chiliec.

related_prs.title: fix(distill): refuse backend: unsloth at config load (#1186)
related_prs.head: de5f77d569f82dc105b3a1539842793998af5d85
related_prs.body:
Part of #1186.

`task: distill` with `backend: unsloth` passed validation, and then the run trained on plain transformers because nothing in the distill path reads the backend. This takes option 1 from the issue: `validate_distill_compat` now refuses `unsloth` the same way it refuses `mlx`, and the error names the supported backend.

I checked `examples/`, `templates/`, the recipe catalog and the docs for any shipped config that pairs `distill` with `unsloth`, and found none, so there is nothing to warn about before refusing.

**Tests** (in `tests/test_v0520.py`, next to the existing mlx test):
- `test_validate_distill_compat_unsloth`: the helper raises.
- `test_soup_config_refuses_distill_on_unsloth`: `SoupConfig` raises `ValidationError` at load.

Both fail with `DID NOT RAISE` when the new branch is removed, and pass with it.

**Validation**
- `pytest tests/test_v0520.py -k "distill_compat or distill_on_unsloth" --no-cov`: 2 failed before the change, 4 passed after.
- Every `tests/test_*.py` that mentions distill, run before and after the change: the only difference is these two tests going green. My env had no `[train]` extra (no torch/trl), so 177 torch-dependent tests fail the same way on both sides. I did not run the full suite with the training stack installed.
- `soup doctor --config` on a `task: distill` + `backend: unsloth` config now prints the refusal and exits 2 instead of reporting the config as clean.
- `ruff check` on both touched files passes.

Item 3 of #1186, tests only.

#1746 gates the "unsloth is installed" tip on whether the config still loads with `backend: unsloth`, which covers this item. This PR keeps only the tests for it.

- `tests/test_issue1186_unsloth_tip_gated.py`: `--dry-run` with unsloth reported as installed. The tip shows for `sft`, and not for `distill` or `classifier`. Each case asserts the config loaded first ("Training Setup" panel), so the tip is not missing for the wrong reason.

On current main the three tests pass. With the `_unsloth_tip_applies(cfg)` gate replaced by `cfg.backend == "transformers"`, the `distill` and `classifier` cases fail. `ruff check` is clean.

related_prs.title: test(config): name the refused and alias categories, and check every shipped config
related_prs.head: 6c9e598cd61a1c9e13a0856e19a2b5a946acd39c
related_prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Refs #1814: parts 1 and 4 of the claim (the guard categories and the shipped-config test). `training.forgetting_threshold` (part 2) needs a per-entry staged deadline, since `STAGED_FIELD_SEVERITY` is one global switch; and `training.warmup_auto` (part 3) waits for your call on the issue. Both come in a follow-up.

**Guard categories** (`tests/test_issue748_config_fields_reach_a_consumer.py`). `KNOWN_UNCONSUMED` mixed fields a user can set to no effect with four that a schema validator does read. They move to two named categories, each entry naming the validator that consumes it:

| Category | Field | Validator |
|---|---|---|
| `REFUSED_AT_LOAD` | `training.packing_cross_doc_attn_mask` | `TrainingConfig._validate_cross_doc_attn_mask` |
| `VALIDATOR_ALIASES` | `training.load_in_16bit` | `TrainingConfig._validate_load_in_aliases` (rewrites `quantization` to `none`) |
| `VALIDATOR_ALIASES` | `training.llm_int8` | `SoupConfig._validate_llm_int8_alias` (asserts `8bit`) |
| `VALIDATOR_ALIASES` | `training.unsloth_bnb_4bit` | `SoupConfig._validate_unsloth_bnb_4bit_compat` (asserts unsloth + `4bit`) |

- The orphan check, the stale-name check, the now-wired check and both reason checks run over all three (`GUARDED`). The `KNOWN_UNCONSUMED` pin goes **36 → 32**, so it counts only silently inert fields; the categories get their own exact pins (1 and 3) and must not overlap.
- Each category entry is checked, not trusted (`TestTheNamedCategoriesAreTrue`): the named validator exists; `packing_cross_doc_attn_mask: true` is refused naming the field; `load_in_16bit: true` with `quantization: 4bit` loads as `none`; `llm_int8: true` is refused with `4bit` and loads with `8bit`; `unsloth_bnb_4bit: true` is refused on transformers and loads on unsloth + `4bit`.

**Shipped configs** (`tests/test_shipped_configs_set_no_inert_field.py`). Every recipe in `RECIPES` and every template is loaded, and the test fails, naming the config and the field, when one sets a field in `KNOWN_UNCONSUMED`, a staged field, or a deprecated value (recorded from the same `SoupConfig` construction the loader performs, since the loader turns those warnings into console lines). All 191 pass today (the issue counted 170 recipes at v0.76.0; the catalog has grown), and a floor on the count keeps the loop from passing over nothing. Each of the three detectors is shown to fire on a config that trips it.

**Mutation:** dropping the `llm_int8` alias entry fails the orphan check (and the pin); removing the `8bit` check inside `_validate_llm_int8_alias` fails its category test. `tests/test_issue808_staged_config_fields.py`, `test_issue1272_cache_refusal_reason.py` and `test_issue799_autopilot_unwired_gates.py`, which import `KNOWN_UNCONSUMED`, pass unchanged (154 with the guard file).

Test-only change, no user-visible impact, so no changelog fragment.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / cleanup
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests

## Checklist

- [x] `ruff check src/soup_cli/ scripts/ tests/` passes
- [x] `pytest tests/ -v` passes — the two files and the importers above; full-suite result follows in a comment
- [x] Updated relevant docs (`README.md` and the matching page under `docs/`) if needed — none needed, nothing user-facing changes
- [x] Added a changelog fragment, or this change has no user-visible impact — no user-visible impact
